correctness.rationale: The published two-particle stable equivalence applies because the graph is cubic and has girth six. Independently reconstructed exact cubical cellular boundaries satisfy d1*d2=0, with 120/336/228 cells, Smith factors 207 ones and one two for d2 and d1 rank119. Complete canonical enumeration yields 400 simple cycles and exactly 111 disjoint pairs. All torus columns have zero integer boundary. The larger 48-element hexagon-torus orbit contains 20 columns with an explicit integer coordinate minor of determinant +1. Because kernel(d2) is primitive of rank 20, these are an integral basis; each length-class quotient follows from the full integer Smith factors. The automorphism enumeration is complete (96), and independent direct action on the 20 basis classes verifies the same character distribution as the Lefschetz computation. No infinite extension is claimed.

value.rationale: For a canonical highly symmetric sparse nonplanar cubic graph of girth six, the result identifies the smallest geometric torus carriers of every second-homology class, shows a single 48-element automorphism orbit generates all integral H2, and distinguishes precise free versus parity-defective lattices of longer natural cycle pairs. The vanishing full-group fixed subspace adds equivariant information not determined by ranks. These are natural geometric/integral questions precisely because nonplanar graph braid groups do not generally admit planar torus-generation statements; the exact coefficients have concrete use for cycle-product generators and comparisons in graph braid topology.
